decisions.text: Real connector and cable: the opened FX505 laptop we already have is the source of truth; Shiven measures from the sheet in item 1.
Deployment arm: no Staubli work now; the Meca500 and LR Mate are the cell.
Force guards 4 / 12 / 10 N stay provisional until measured on the real connector.
Gripper open and close are chain steps; policies output arm motion plus one phase-done bit (FORGE style). Same interface for ACT and for PPO with SGS.
A small test suite locks the twin's fixed defaults and the nine-variant pass.

Approved: Nano25 SI-125-3; twin fixes (weld-off, zeroed guards, pinch loop, mesh interference, horn check, figures); Isaac items 1 to 5 plus RoboSimStudio A, B, C; commit to shiven/ffc-twin; use janus GPU; privileged critic allowed; truth-labelled success head allowed.

items.title: Connector modelled from photos
items.issue: Slot height, floor, depth to the seat, roof, housing depth, the lid and the contact preload are marked ESTIMATE in the twin. The CON3104 maker and part are unverified. Every pass in the twin rests on this geometry.

rows: what to measure on the opened FX505

depth from the mouth to the seat
callipers on a scrap cable, insert to the stop
housing depth (front to back) and height
lid: thickness, hinge position from the back, open angle at the stop
macro photo with a ruler in frame
1.35 mm bar hinged 0.3 mm below its top, 100 deg
lid front-edge overhang over the slot (what the lip hooks)
CON3104 on the board, maker unknown
cable: width, stiffener thickness and length, body thickness, mass
cable rest angle out of the deck slot and height of the tip above the board
distance deck slot to connector mouth
parts standing beside the connector within 25 mm (SO-DIMM, rail)
photo from above with a ruler

items.fix: Measure the opened FX505 with callipers and macro photos (sheet below), identify the connector part from its markings, put the measured numbers into the twin, re-run all variants.

hero.text: The twin's connector as the west bench camera sees it at the moment the tip reaches the mouth. Every dimension of this housing, slot and lid is an estimate from photos.

items.title: Cable from a photo
items.issue: 28 mm width, 0.3 mm stiffener, 13 mm stiffener length, 0.14 mm body, bend memory and mass are estimates read off a photo scaled against the SO-DIMM slot.
items.fix: Measure width, stiffener thickness and length, body thickness; weigh the cable; cantilever sag test for bending stiffness; update the twin.

hero.text: The twin's connector as the west bench camera sees it at the moment the tip reaches the mouth. Every dimension of this housing, slot and lid is an estimate from photos.

items.title: Force numbers are design choices
items.issue: The 1 to 3 N seat rise, the 4 N slide guard, the 7 N push and the 10 N press come from the twin's contact springs (0.05 mm proud, soft). The sensor spec and the guards were sized against them.
items.fix: Hand-fixture force trace on the real connector with a kitchen-scale load cell: insertion force vs depth, lid push and press. Keep the guards provisional (decision 4).

hero.text: The run whose contact forces set the 1 to 3 N seat rise and the 4, 12 and 10 N guards. Those forces come from the twin's soft contact springs, not from a measured connector.

items.title: Precision budget partly assumed
items.issue: Hand-eye 20 to 40 um and the camera term in the 0.06 to 0.1 mm budget are assumptions.
items.fix: Camera calibration in the hardware phase (Isaac item 9). Until then the budget is labelled as assumed on the final page.

items.title: Cable held by a weld during the slide
items.issue: The expert welds the stiffener to the tool once grasped (FFC_WELD defaults on). Friction grip was never tested. Servo tool pinch 4.1 N against about 4.9 N friction capacity at the 4 N guard.
items.fix: Run all nine variants with the weld off; raise the servo tool pinch toward 8 N if it slips; keep weld-off as the default.

hero.text: Servo tool run as validated today: during the slide the stiffener is welded to the tool (FFC_WELD=1). The weld-off re-run is in progress; its video will sit beside this one.

items.title: Pinch loop not simulated
items.issue: Cell P is geometry only; the pad is a 20 N/mm position spring. The pages claim a closed loop on cell P.
items.fix: Add a pinch force sensor between pad and carrier, a servo-like position stage with the pad's compliance, and a close-until-5 N loop in the expert; re-run the servo variants.

items.title: Force guards never zeroed
items.issue: guarded() stops on the raw wrist force magnitude. The bought stacks pass partly because the stack weight points along the flange axis.
items.fix: Bias the reading at the start of each guarded move (what the real controller does); re-run all nine variants and compare stop depths.

fix_evidence.text: guarded() now reads the wrist force relative to its value at the start of the move (FFC_ZERO_GUARD=1 default); all nine variants are re-running with the weld off.

items.title: Printed parts excluded from the interference check
items.issue: The schematic's zero-overlap claim covers boxes and cylinders only; body, carriers, rocker and cover meshes were skipped.
items.fix: cadquery boolean intersections of every STEP part pair at open, closed and the hard stop; report volumes.

hero.text: The schematic's interference panel (right) checks boxes and cylinders only; the grey printed meshes are not in that check yet.

items.title: The expert is privileged
items.issue: The expert reads the true tip pose before the slide. The camera-based tip estimator built for the Pi cable (September, ffc-twin env.py) was never ported to this cell, so no sensor-only episodes exist.
items.fix: Port the estimator (bench-camera edge estimate with latency and noise, dead reckoning when occluded); run the expert on it; report the capture region.

items.title: No latency, noise or controller model in the twin
items.issue: The arm is driven kinematically; no 8 ms Stream Motion cycle, no Meca500 command cycle, no F/T noise.
items.fix: Covered by the Isaac cell (controller and sensor models). Twin numbers are labelled geometry checks on every page.

items.title: Yaw correction lightly tested
items.issue: The expert's yaw measurement and J6 turn were tested at 0.8 and 2 degrees only.
items.fix: Sweep yaw -3 to +3 degrees in the weld-off re-run; report pass per angle.

items.title: Nano25 calibration does not exist
items.issue: SI-62.5-1.5 is on every page, in review.py, parts.json and the submitted ATI RFQ. ATI lists SI-125-3 and SI-250-6 for the Nano25.
items.fix: SI-125-3 everywhere: 125 N / 500 N / 3 N m, resolution 1/48 N, 1/16 N, 1/1320 N m; correction in the ATI follow-up; re-run the review.
items.research: ATI's Nano25 page lists only SI-125-3 and SI-250-6 (checked 2026-10-14). The 12 N push at the 65 mm lever is 0.78 N m: 26 percent of SI-125-3's 3 N m. Resolution 1/48 N is 5 times finer than the 0.1 N the guards need.
items.verification: review.py SENSORS, parts.json, the final page, the blueprint and the quote pack now say SI-125-3; the final page has zero mentions of 62.5. Compliance row: 0.78 of 3 N m at the push guard. The ATI follow-up carries the correction.

verification_evidence.text: torque at the sensor at the 12 N push guard: 26 percent of range (was written as 52 percent of a 1.5 N m range that does not exist)

items.title: MEGP finger mass at the limit
items.issue: Mecademic allows 20 g per finger; the printed fingers weigh 19 and 20 g by volume.
items.fix: Trim (thinner plate or lighter infill) or confirm the limit's basis with Mecademic.
